theme: शीतोष्ण और मान-अपमान में स्थिरता: योग का आंतरिक संतुलन। / Stability amid heat, cold, honour, and dishonour: the inner balance of yoga.
context: Krishna has already described the yogi’s seat, restraint of mind and senses, and the disciplined practice of meditation. In this verse, he identifies the sign of true steadiness: the inner Self remains centered even when life brings opposites and reactions.
contextHindi: कृष्ण ने पहले योगी के आसन, मन की एकाग्रता, संयम और एकांत की तैयारी का वर्णन किया। अब वे बताते हैं कि असली योग की पहचान क्या है: मन और आत्मा सभी विपरीत अनुभवों में एक जैसा स्थिर रहता है।
sanskritDevanagari:
जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः |
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ||६-७||
transliteration:
jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya paramātmā samāhitaḥ .
śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu tathā mānāpamānayoḥ ||6-7||

wordByWord.meaning: One whose self is mastered; self-controlled and inwardly disciplined.
Peaceful, settled, free from agitation and inner turbulence.
The Supreme Self or higher Self, the deepest abiding reality.
Centered, established, harmonized in the inner being.
In cold and heat, pleasure and pain; in the sharp swings of ordinary experience.
In honour and dishonour; in status, praise, and humiliation.

spokenHindi: यह श्लोक योगी की आंतरिक स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। जितात्मा यानी जिसके भीतर मन का नियंत्रण है, और प्रशान्त आत्मा यानी जो गहन शांति में स्थापित है, उसके लिए परमात्मा समाहित रहता है। इसका अर्थ यह नहीं कि उसे कोई दुख नहीं होगा; बल्कि उसके भीतर वही स्थिर सत्य है जो शीत और उष्ण, सुख और दुख, मान और अपमान—इन सब विपरीत अनुभवों में भी अचल रहता है। यह एक मानसिक तटस्थता नहीं है, बल्कि आत्म-प्रकाश का गहरा सामंजस्य है। जब हम किसी घटना को अपने अहंकार से ग्रहण करते हैं, तब हम तुरंत प्रतिक्रिया करते हैं; लेकिन योगी भीतर देखता है कि इन सभी भिन्न अवस्थाओं से आत्मा असंग और अटल है। इसलिए यह श्लोक हमें सिखाता है: स्थिरता बाहरी जीवन की परिस्थितियों से नहीं आती, बल्कि अपने भीतर स्वयं को देखने की क्षमता से आती है। बिना आत्म-निरीक्षण के, हम हर दर्द और प्रशंसा से घबराते हैं।
clearEnglish: This verse describes the state of a person whose inner life is not thrown off balance by opposites. Jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya refers to a self-controlled and peaceful person, and paramātmā samāhitaḥ means the Supreme Self is settled, centered, or harmonized within. The verse does not say that a yogi never feels heat, pain, praise, or insult. It says that such experiences do not become the governing force of the mind. The higher Self remains present as the inner witness. In practical terms, this is not emotional numbness. It is a disciplined inward steadiness: when a person loses status, receives praise, faces discomfort, or encounters criticism, the deeper consciousness does not collapse into reaction. That kind of balance is not achieved by pretending nothing hurts. It is cultivated by repeated attention, dispassion, and willingness to see the self beneath the ego’s drama. In modern life, this is the ability to pause before reacting, to keep dignity without becoming rigid, and to live from self-knowledge rather than from external validation.

interpretationPerspectives.label: Text
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse states a condition of inner balance: a self-controlled and peaceful person has the Supreme Self centered amid cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour. It describes a stable inner reference point, not the absence of experience.

interpretationPerspectives.label: Inference
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A person who can remain steady in opposites is not merely suppressing emotion; they are learning not to let reaction define identity. That is a practical discipline of awareness, humility, and self-regulation.

practicalApplication.label: Pause before reaction
practicalApplication.text: When praise, criticism, comfort, or discomfort arrives, stop for ten seconds and ask: am I responding from the ego or from the deeper Self? This small pause can reduce impulsive speech and protect inner steadiness.

practicalApplication.label: Inner witness
practicalApplication.text: Notice which experiences most easily disturb your mind: heat, cold, insult, praise, boredom, status, or loss. Practice observing them without immediately identifying with them.

reflectionQuestion: When praise or criticism changes my mood, what does it say about where I am placing my sense of self?
reflectionQuestionHindi: जब तारीफ या निंदा मेरे मनोदशा को बदल देती है, तो इससे पता चलता है कि मैं अपने आप को कहाँ रखता हूँ?
